text: CPR should begin immediately and adrenaline 1 mg should be given by intravenous or intraosseous injection every 3 to 5 minutes; in the USA, a single dose of vaso- pressin may be given instead of either the first or second dose of adrenaline if the patient is in asystole.4 For asystole a single dose of atropine 3 mg intravenously is also given to block vagal activity;5,6 in the American guidelines4 atro- pine is recommended in repeated doses of 1 mg to a total maximum dose of 3 mg. Other drugs (such as buffering agents) may be considered. Cardiac pacing may be started once there is evidence of electrical activity. Resuscitation should generally continue for at least 20 to 30 minutes from the time of collapse; it is not usually prolonged as recovery rarely occurs after 15 to 20 minutes of asystole if there has been no response. For children with asystole or electromechanical dissocia- tion, the initial dose of adrenaline recommended is 10 micrograms/kg given by intravenous or intraosseous injection; as for ventricular fibrillation, higher doses have been used subsequently but are not generally recommend- ed. Alternatively, adrenaline may be given by the endotra- cheal route in doses of 100 micrograms/kg. Atropine is not generally used and a precordial thump is not recommend- ed. 1.
